title: Abstract cell complex: combinatorial (poset) formalisation
body_html:
Abstract cell complex

The paper's §2.1 setup — a locally finite regular CW complex with a cellular $G$-action, see Locally finite regular CW complex with cellular G-action — is topological. The Lean formalisation extracts the purely combinatorial content that §§2–4 actually use: the face poset plus a dimension function. This "abstract cell complex" is what all downstream Lean definitions (sheaves, cosheaves, QFD, induction, orientation, chain complex) are built on.

Debundled API

The Lean library debundles the setup into four independent typeclass layers, applied one at a time as needed:

Layer Kind Carries
AbstractCellComplex X data class dimension function dim : X → ℕ and its monotonicity axioms
IsLocallyFinite X Prop mixin each cell has finitely many faces and finitely many cofaces
GCellComplex G X Prop class the requirement that a MulAction G X is cellular
Subcomplex X structure a face-closed subset of the cells

A "$G$-cellular complex of locally finite type" is spelled out as

lean (X : Type*) [PartialOrder X] [AbstractCellComplex X] [IsLocallyFinite X] [MulAction G X] [GCellComplex G X]

with no layer bundling any of the others.

AbstractCellComplex

Add to [PartialOrder X]:

  • a dimension function dim : X → ℕ;
  • strict monotonicity: a proper face has strictly smaller dimension;
  • face existence: every cell of positive dimension has a face of dimension one less (without this axiom one could have a "2-cell" attached directly to a vertex with no edges in between, which is not the face poset of any regular CW complex).

Formally:

$$ \mathrm{dim}_{-\!\mathrm{lt}}\!: E \le F \wedge E \ne F \Rightarrow \mathrm{dim}\,E < \mathrm{dim}\,F. $$

$$ \exists\,\mathrm{face}_{-\!\mathrm{dim}_{-\!\mathrm{pred}}}\!: 0 < \mathrm{dim}\,F \Rightarrow \exists\,E,\ E < F \wedge \mathrm{dim}\,E + 1 = \mathrm{dim}\,F. $$

IsLocallyFinite

A Prop mixin, independent of AbstractCellComplex:

  • $\{F : F \le E\}$ is finite for every $E$ (finitely many faces);
  • $\{F : E \le F\}$ is finite for every $E$ (finitely many cofaces).

Both together formalise "each point has a neighbourhood meeting only finitely many cells" for a regular CW complex. In the abstract poset setting the two are independent, but for a regular CW complex the geometric "locally finite" assumption delivers both at once, so we bundle them in one Prop class.

GCellComplex

A Prop class asserting that a MulAction G X is cellular:

  • $G$ preserves the face relation: $E \le F \Rightarrow g \cdot E \le g \cdot F$;
  • $G$ preserves dimension: $\mathrm{dim}(g \cdot E) = \mathrm{dim}\,E$.

The cell complex data and the MulAction are not bundled into this class: both are separate typeclass inputs. GCellComplex G X is purely the compatibility requirement on top.

Subcomplex

A cellular subcomplex is a face-closed subset of the cells. Modelled after mathlib's Subgroup / Submonoid idiom: it holds a carrier : Set X field and is SetLike, so the usual E ∈ S notation is available.

Relationship to the paper

Every §2.1 topological ingredient is either:

  • retained in the Lean abstraction (face relation, dimension, locally-finite bound, cellular action, subcomplex);
  • abstracted away because it is not used combinatorially (topology on $|X|$, open/closed cells, attaching maps).

Downstream:

  • Sheaves and cosheaves (Sheaves and cosheaves on X as functor categories) are functors on the face poset.
  • G-equivariant (co)sheaves (G-equivariant sheaves and cosheaves) are extra structure on such functors.
  • QFD and induction (Quasi-fundamental domain, [[node:equivariant_sheaves.induction_GxP_X]]) are stated at this cell-poset level throughout.
  • The ∂² = 0 cellular chain complex ([[node:representations.chain_complex_C_dot]]) uses only AbstractCellComplex + IsLocallyFinite + Orientation.
